A regeneration.

en: Worthy of reverence or respect.
Showing or granting reverence or respect.
A member of the Christian clergy; a minister.

reverend.ety: Borrowed from Middle French révérend, from Old French, from Latin future passive participle reverendus (“that is to be respected”), from deponent verb revereor (“to honor, revere”).

note.ja: ラテン語 reverendus（敬われるべき）から。revereri（敬う）。revere と同じ。

en: The deteriorated state of iron or steel as a result of moisture and oxidation; it consists mostly of iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide) and i…
A similar substance based on another metal.
To oxidize, especially of iron or steel.
To cause to oxidize.

rust.ety:
From Middle English rust, rost, roust, from Old English rust, rūst (“rust”), from Proto-West Germanic *rust, from Proto-Germanic *rustaz (“rust”), from Proto-Indo-European *rudʰso- (“red”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewdʰ- (“red”).
Cognate with Scots roust (“rust”), Saterland Frisian rust (“rust”), West Frisian roast (“rust”), Dutch roest (“rust”), German Rost (“rust”), Danish rust (“rust”), Swedish rost (“rust”), Norwegian rust, ryst (“rust”), Finnish ruoste, Estonian rooste. Related to red.

ex.en: Hey, rust is eating away the metal.
ex.ja: ほら、錆で金属がどんどん腐食しているよ。

ex.en: Better wear out than rust out.
ex.ja: さびつかせるよりもすり切らしたほうがいい。

ex.en: It is better to wear out than to rust out.
ex.ja: さびつかせてしまうより使い古す方が良い。

note.ja: 古英語 rūst から。red（赤）と同じ祖先。「赤くなったもの」→「さび」。

en: Tasting of salt.
Containing salt.

salty.ety:
PIE word
 *sḗh₂l
Inherited from Middle English salti. Equivalent to salt + -y.
Compare Saterland Frisian soaltig (“salty”), West Frisian sâltich (“salty”), Dutch zoutig (“salty”), German Low German soltig (“salty”), German salzig (“salty”).
(coarse; irritated, annoyed): Referencing the sharp, 'spicy' flavor of salt.
(indignant): Perhaps implying the person is a crybaby, shedding salty tears, or derived from the preceding.

ex.en: This is too sweet and that is too salty.
ex.ja: これは甘すぎるし、あれは塩辛すぎる。

ex.en: This water is a little salty.
ex.ja: この水は少し塩辛い。

ex.en: It's less salty than we thought.
ex.ja: 思ったより塩分は少ないんですよ。

note.ja: salt（塩）+ -y。「塩辛い」。

en: Intense study of someone or something.
Thorough inspection of a situation or a case.

scrutiny.ety: From Middle English scrutiny, from Medieval Latin scrūtinium (“a search, an inquiry”), from Vulgar Latin scrūtor (“to search or examine thoroughly”), from Late Latin scrūta (“rubbish, broken trash”), from an extension of Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to cut”).

ex.en: Corporate political donations are coming under heavy scrutiny.
ex.ja: 企業の政治献金は厳しい検査の対象になっています。

note.ja: ラテン語 scrutinium（調べること）から。scruta（ぼろ切れ）をあさって探すことから。「綿密な調査」。

en: The act of taking possession, as by force or right of law.
The state of being seized or of having been taken.
To experience an epileptic seizure.

en: Blood serum used as a blood product, in the practice of medicine: blood serum from the tissues of immunized animals (human or nonhuman), …
A watery liquid from animal tissue, especially one that moistens the surface of serous membranes or that is exuded by such membranes when…

From Latin serum (“whey”). Cognates include French sérum, Spanish suero, Italian siere, siero, Portuguese soro. Doublet of suero.

note.ja: ラテン語 serum（乳清・水っぽい液）から。「血清」。

en: Being only one of a larger population; single, individual.
Being the only one of the kind; unique.
A form of a word that refers to only one person or thing.
That which is not general; a specific determinate instance.

singular.ety: From Middle English singuler, from Old French, from Latin singulāris (“alone of its kind”), from Latin singulus (“single”).

ex.en: The word "every" is treated as singular.
ex.ja: everyは単数扱いになります。

ex.en: He is a boy of singular intelligence.
ex.ja: 彼は並はずれた知能の持ち主である。

ex.en: She is a woman of singular beauty.
ex.ja: 彼女はまれにみる美しい女性だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 singularis（ひとつの）から。singulus。「単数の」→ 唯一の「並外れた・奇妙な」。single と同じ。

en: A runner or blade, usually of steel, with a frame shaped to fit the sole of a shoe, made to be fastened under the foot, and used for glid…
The act of skateboarding
To move along a surface (ice or ground) using skates.
To skateboard.
Pertaining to the technique of skating.

skate.ety: Back-formation from Dutch schaats, from Middle Dutch schāetse, from Old Northern French escache (“a stilt, trestle”) (compare French échasse and English scatch), from a Germanic language, perhaps Frankish *skakkjā (“stilt”, literally “thing that moves”), related to *skakan (“to shake, swing”).

ex.en: It seems like yesterday that we skated together.
ex.ja: いっしょにスケートをしたのが、まるで昨日のことみたいです。

ex.en: It is safe to skate on this lake.
ex.ja: この湖でスケートをしても安全だ。

ex.en: The ice is too thin to skate on.
ex.ja: 氷が薄すぎてスケートができません。

note.ja: オランダ語 schaats（すべるもの）から。「スケートをする」。魚の「エイ」は北欧語 skata からで別語。

en: The plot of a story; one of several within a story, usually interwoven.
A narrative description of a given modeling scenario, highlighting its main characteristics and underlying technical and socioeconomic dr…

storyline.ety: From story + line. The climate science usage is defined in the IPCC WG III AR5 report (2014).

ex.en: Her latest album is a tour de force. It even has a storyline.
ex.ja: 今回発売されたアルバムは、ストーリー仕立てになっていて力作だ。

note.ja: story（物語）+ line（筋）。「物語の筋」。

en: Any domestic animal that lacks an enclosure, proper place, or company, but that instead wanders at large or is lost; an estray.
A person who is lost.
To wander, as from a direct course; to deviate, or go out of the way.
To wander from company or outside proper limits; to rove or roam at large; to go astray.
Having gone astray; strayed; wandering.
In the wrong place; misplaced.

stray.ety: From Middle English stray, strey, from Anglo-Norman estray, stray, Old French estrai, from the verb (see below).

ex.en: Tom only looked after the stray for 6 days.
ex.ja: トムは、六日間だけ迷子の犬を預かることにしました。

ex.en: The stray dog suddenly came at the child.
ex.ja: 野犬は突然子供に飛びかかった。

ex.en: A lost dog strayed into our neighborhood yesterday.
ex.ja: 道に迷った犬が昨日私たちの近所に迷い込んできた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 estraier（さまよう）から。ラテン語 extra vagare（外をさまよう）とされる。「迷子の・はぐれる」。astray（道に迷って）も同じ。

en: Financial support or assistance, such as a grant.

subsidy.ety: From Middle English subsidy, subsidie, from Anglo-Norman subsidee, subsidie, from Old French subside, from Latin subsidium (support, assistance), from subsido from sub- (“below”) + sīdō (“sit”).

note.ja: ラテン語 subsidium（予備軍・援助）から。sub（後ろに）+ sedere（座る）。「後ろに控えて助けるもの」→「補助金」。subsidiary と同じ。

en: An optional light meal consumed shortly before going to bed.
Any meal eaten in the evening; dinner eaten in the evening, rather than at noon.
To consume a snack before going to bed.
To eat dinner.

supper.ety: From Middle English soper, from Old French soper, from sope (“soup”). Compare French souper.

ex.en: We could eat supper before it, couldn't we?
ex.ja: 食事をしてからでも間に合いますね？

ex.en: After supper, I always find myself falling asleep.
ex.ja: 夕食後、いつも眠りそうになるんです。

ex.en: I watched the news on TV after supper.
ex.ja: 夕食後テレビのニュースを見た。

note.ja: 古フランス語 soper（夕食をとる）から。soup（スープ）と同じ語源。「スープを飲む軽い食事」→「夕食」。

en: A person who is always very kind.
A person very much liked or loved by someone, especially when both partners are young.

sweetheart.ety: From Middle English swete heorte, swete hert (term of endearment); equivalent to sweet + heart.

ex.en: To tell the truth, sweetheart, I'm not at all interested.
ex.ja: 正直に言いますよ、ねえあなた、私は全く興味がないのです。

ex.en: I call my sweetheart darling.
ex.ja: 私は恋人を「ダーリン」と呼びます。

note.ja: sweet（甘い・いとしい）+ heart（心）。「いとしい人」→「恋人」。

en: Embedded within and spread throughout and affecting a whole system, group, body, economy, market, or society.
Pertaining to an entire organism.

note.ja: system（体系・体）+ -ic。「全身の・体系的な・構造的な」。

en: A frequency or rate.
A move which is part of one's own plan or strategy and forces, e.g. by means of a check or attacking a piece, the opponent to make a move…

tempo.ety:
Borrowed from Italian tempo, from Latin tempus (“time”). Doublet of tense.
(truck or cargo van): A genericized trademark, originally associated with the manufacturer Vidal & Sohn Tempo-Werke GmbH.

note.ja: イタリア語 tempo（時）から。ラテン語 tempus。「時の刻み方」→「テンポ」。temporary と同じ。

en: Of this, that, or it.
From that circumstance or origin; therefrom, thence.

thereof.ety: From Middle English thereof, therof, ther-of, ther of, from Old English þǣrof; equivalent to there + of. Compare Swedish därav.

ex.en: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
ex.ja: 語りえないことについては、沈黙するほかない。

note.ja: there（それ）+ of。「それの・その」。法律文などで使う硬い言い方。

en: Needing to drink water or any liquid that can supply water.
Craving alcohol; especially, experiencing some alcohol withdrawal.
One who is thirsty (for a drink, sex, alcohol, etc.).
Thirst.

thirsty.ety: From Middle English thirsty, from Old English þurstiġ, from Proto-West Germanic *þurstug. Equivalent to thirst + -y. Cognate with Dutch dorstig, German durstig.

ex.en: I'm thirsty. Please give me a cold drink.
ex.ja: 喉が渇いています。何か冷たい飲物を下さい。

ex.en: Why didn't you tell Tom you were thirsty?
ex.ja: 何で喉が渇いてること、トムに言わなかったの？

ex.en: I am thirsty. Give me something to drink!
ex.ja: 喉がカラカラ。なんか飲み物！

note.ja: thirst（渇き）+ -y。「のどが渇いた」→「渇望している」。

en: A stick of wood or plant fibres twisted together, with one end soaked in a flammable substance such as resin or tallow and set on fire, w…
A similarly shaped implement with a replaceable supply of flammable material; specifically, a pole with a lamp at one end.
To illuminate or provide (a place) with torches (noun etymology 1, noun sense 1).
To intentionally destroy (something) by setting it on fire, especially when committing arson in furtherance of some other criminal act (e…

ex.en: It was identified by telescope as a torch.
ex.ja: 望遠鏡で見ると、それはたいまつであることがわかった。

ex.en: She shone her torch onto the floor before us.
ex.ja: 懐中電灯をつけて、足元を照らしてくれた。

ex.en: Place some torches so that mobs don't spawn.
ex.ja: モブがスポーンしないように松明を置いといて。

note.ja: 古フランス語 torche（ねじった藁）から。ラテン語 torquere（ねじる）。「たいまつ」。torture、torque と同じ tort。

en: A turbine.
With rapidly-increasing blind levels.
Causing or relating to increased speed.
To autofire.

note.ja: turbocharger の短縮。ラテン語 turbo（渦・こま）。turbine、disturb と同じ。

en: Not changed or altered; remaining in an original state.

From un- + changed.

ex.en: The situation remains unchanged.
ex.ja: 状況は相変わらずそのままだ。

ex.en: The packaging has been updated but the contents are unchanged.
ex.ja: 箱はリニューアルしたけど中身は変わらない。

note.ja: un（否定）+ change（変える）+ -ed。「変わらない」。

en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.
Capable of being accepted or excused under the circumstances; permissible.

understandable.ety: From Middle English understondable, equivalent to understand + -able.

ex.en: His anger is understandable.
ex.ja: 彼の、怒りも理解できる。

ex.en: She failed the exam, which was understandable.
ex.ja: 彼女は試験に失敗したが、それは無理もなかった。

ex.en: Thank you so much for your always easily understandable explanations.
ex.ja: いつも分かりやすい説明をありがとうございます。

note.ja: understand + -able。「理解できる・もっともな」。

en: Vertical; erect.
In its proper orientation; not overturned.
In or into an upright position.
On one's feet (as opposed to in a wheelchair).
Any vertical part of a structure, especially a part that provides support.
A goal post.
To set upright or stand back up (something that has fallen).

upright.ety: From Middle English upright, uppryght, upriht, from Old English upriht (“upright; erect”), from Proto-Germanic *upprehtaz, equivalent to up- + right. Cognate with Saterland Frisian apgjucht (“upright”), West Frisian oprjocht (“upright”), Dutch oprecht (“upright”), German Low German uprecht (“upright”), German aufrecht (“upright”), Swedish upprätt (“upright”), Icelandic uppréttur (“upright”).

ex.en: Stand upright when I'm talking to you.
ex.ja: 私が君に向かって話している時はまっすぐ立っていなさい。

ex.en: The soul of commerce is upright dealing.
ex.ja: 商業の生命は正直な取引である。

ex.en: An empty bag can't stand upright.
ex.ja: ない袖は振れぬ。

note.ja: up（上へ）+ right（まっすぐな）。「直立した」→「正直な」。

en: A popular revolt that attempts to overthrow a government or its policies; an insurgency or insurrection.

ex.en: His analysis of the causes of the uprising was correct.
ex.ja: 暴動の原因についての彼の分析は正しかった。

ex.en: The government acted boldly to deal with the outlaw uprising.
ex.ja: 政府は無法者たちの激突に対して大胆に対処した。

note.ja: up（上へ）+ rising（立ち上がること）。「立ち上がること」→「蜂起・反乱」。

en: Overly proud of oneself, especially concerning appearance; having a high opinion of one's own accomplishments with slight reason.
Having no real substance, value, or importance; empty; void; worthless; unsatisfying.

vain.ety: From Middle English veyn, from Old French vain, from Latin vānus (“empty”).

ex.en: I tried to get it, but in vain.
ex.ja: 手に入れようとしたが、無駄だった。

ex.en: He tried in vain to open the box.
ex.ja: 彼はその箱を開けようとしたがだめだった。

ex.en: I tried in vain to explain the reason.
ex.ja: 私はその理由を説明しようとしたが、無駄だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 vanus（空っぽの）から。「むだな」→ 中身がないのに「うぬぼれた」。vanity、vanish と同じ。

en: That which is vain, futile, or worthless; that which is of no value, use or profit.
Excessive pride in or admiration of one's own abilities, appearance, achievements, or possessions.

vanity.ety: From va(i)n + -ity, from Middle English vanite, from Old French vanité, from Latin vānitas, from vānus, whence English vain. Doublet of vanitas.

ex.en: She's always looking at herself in the mirror - What vanity.
ex.ja: 彼女はいつも鏡で自分の姿を見ている、何といううぬぼれだ。

ex.en: Tom was a ball of vanity.
ex.ja: トムは虚栄心の塊のような人だった。

ex.en: I can't find my vanity case.
ex.ja: 私の化粧ケースがみつからないのです。

note.ja: ラテン語 vanus（空っぽの）から。van + ity。中身のないこと →「虚栄心・むなしさ」。vain（無駄な）も同じ。

Any instrument of the violin family, always inclusive of violins, violas and cellos, and sometimes further including the double bass.
To play on, or as if on, a violin.

ex.ja: 君はバイオリンを毎日練習するべきだ。

ex.en: By the way, do you play the violin?
ex.ja: ところで、君はバイオリンを弾きますか。

ex.en: Are you sure that Tom plays the violin?
ex.ja: 本当にトムはバイオリンを弾けるんですか？

note.ja: where + by。「それによって」。thereby と同じ作り。

en: The act of speaking in a quiet voice, especially without vibration of the vocal cords; the sound thus produced.
A rumor.
To speak softly or under one's breath, so as to be heard only by one near at hand; to utter words without sonant breath; to talk without …
To say (something) softly or under one's breath, so as to be heard only by one near at hand; to utter (something) without sonant breath, …

whisper.ety:
From Middle English whisperen, from Old English hwisprian (“to mutter, murmur, whisper”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwisprōn, from Proto-Germanic *hwisprōną (“to hiss, whistle, whisper”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱweys-, *ḱwey- (“to hiss, whistle, whisper”).
Cognate with Dutch wisperen (“to whisper”), German wispern (“to mumble, whisper”). Related also to Danish hviske (“to whisper”), Icelandic hvískra (“to whisper”), Norwegian Bokmål hviske, kviskre (“to whisper”), Norwegian Nynorsk kviskre, kviskra (“to whisper”), Swedish viska (“to whisper”). More at English whistle.

ex.en: She whispered to me that she was hungry.
ex.ja: 彼女は私に、お腹がすいているとささやいた。

ex.en: I heard my parents whispering last night.
ex.ja: 両親が昨晩ひそひそと話をしているのを聞いた。

ex.en: She spoke to me in a whisper.
ex.ja: 彼女は私に小声で話した。

note.ja: 古英語 hwisprian（ささやく）から。擬音的な語。whistle と同系。

en: Good and important enough to spend time, effort, or money on.

ex.en: It is worthwhile listening to his concert.
ex.ja: 彼のコンサートは聴く価値がある。

ex.en: It is worthwhile to have a try at it.
ex.ja: それは一度やってみる価値がある。

ex.en: It is worthwhile to read this book.
ex.ja: この本は読むだけの価値がある。

note.ja: worth（価値がある）+ while（時間）。「時間をかける価値がある」→「やりがいのある」。

A supposed relation with lavare (“to wash”) is now widely discredited, nor is there probably any relation with Arabic لابة (lāba, “black volcanic rock”). Alternatively, the Romance words are connected with Provençal lavo, lauvo (“flat stone”), from a Vulgar Latin source borrowed from a Celtic language such as Gaulish *lawā, but ultimately of obscure origin; see Proto-Celtic *līwos for details.

ex.en: Can you give me a geological explanation of lava?
ex.ja: 溶岩を地理学的に説明してくれませんか。

ex.en: The volcano shoots out flames and lava.
ex.ja: 火山は炎と溶岩を吹き出す。

note.ja: イタリア語（ナポリ方言）lava（流れ）から。ラテン語 lavare（洗う）。「溶岩」。lavatory（洗面所）と同じ。

en: Having endured for a long period of time.
Having been for a long time

ex.ja: 彼は知事と長年の付き合いです。

en: A piece of material that attracts some metals by magnetism.
An alluring or attractive person or thing.

From Middle English magnete, via Old French magnete, Latin magnēs, magnētem (“lodestone”), from Ancient Greek μαγνῆτις [λίθος] (magnêtis [líthos], “Magnesian [stone]”), either after the Lydian city Magnesia ad Sipylum (modern-day Manisa, Turkey), or after the Greek region of Μαγνησία (Magnēsía) (whence came the colonists who founded the city in Lydia). Related to manganese, magnesia and magnesium.

ex.en: The earth is like a big magnet.
ex.ja: 地球は大きな磁石のようなものです。

ex.en: The magnets on their heads were responsible for that.
ex.ja: 頭の上の磁石がその原因だった。

ex.en: Earth is like a big magnet.
ex.ja: 地球は大きな磁石のようなものです。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 Magnēs lithos（マグネシアの石）から。磁石がとれたマグネシア地方の名。magnesium も同じ。

en: The use of a word, phrase, concept, or set of concepts to refer to something other than its literal meaning, invoking an implicit similar…
A word or phrase used in such implied comparison.
To use a metaphor.
To describe by means of a metaphor.

metaphor.ety: From Middle French métaphore, from Latin metaphora, from Ancient Greek μεταφορά (metaphorá), from μεταφέρω (metaphérō, “to transfer, apply”), from μετά (metá, “with, across, after”) + φέρω (phérō, “to bear, carry”).

ex.en: "He's a tiger when he's angry" is an example of metaphor.
ex.ja: 「怒ると彼はトラになる」というのは隠喩の例である。

ex.en: It's apparently a metaphor for something uncatchable, light of body and fleet of foot.
ex.ja: 捕らえることのできないもの、身軽で素早いもののたとえ、だそうです。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 metaphora（移し替え）から。meta（越えて）+ pherein（運ぶ）。「意味を運び移すこと」→「隠喩」。

en: Somebody whose wealth is at least one million (10⁶) currency units (usually understood to exclude holders of hyperinflated currencies).

millionaire.ety: From French millionnaire. By surface analysis, million + -aire.

ex.en: He lives as if he were a millionaire.
ex.ja: 彼はまるで百万長者のように暮らしている。

ex.en: The millionaire began life as a poor boy.
ex.ja: その大富豪は貧しい少年として生涯を始めた。

ex.en: It is said that he is a millionaire.
ex.ja: 彼は大金持ちだそうだ。

note.ja: million + -aire（〜を持つ人）。フランス語から。「百万長者」。

ja: 無効の（null and void：無効の）

en: A non-existent or empty value or set of values.
Zero quantity of expressions; nothing.
Having no validity; "null and void".
Insignificant.
To return to the null position, setting, etc.
To form nulls, or into nulls, as in a lathe.

null.ety:

Borrowed from Middle French nul, from Latin nūllus.

ex.en: How is Null expressed as a regular expression?
ex.ja: 正規表現でヌルはどのように表されるのでしょうか？

ex.en: This bond is null and void.
ex.ja: この証書は完全に無効である。

note.ja: ラテン語 nullus（何もない）から。ne（否定）+ ullus（何か）。「無効の・ゼロの」。annul（無効にする）も同じ。

en: Used to acknowledge a small mistake or accident.
Used to indicate mild surprise or shock.
A minor mistake or unforeseen difficulty.
To make a mistake; to blunder.

oops.ety: A presumably 'natural' exclamation, attested in writing since 1921. Related to or a variation of whoops (itself attested since 1933). A shortening of whoops-a-daisy, whoopsie-daisy, or oops-a-daisy, which in turn is a mispronunciation of ups-a-daisy or upsy-daisy.

ex.en: "Did you bring the book?" "Oops! I forgot!"
ex.ja: 「本は持ってきた？」「あっ！忘れちゃった！」

ex.en: Oops, my pen has run out of ink.
ex.ja: おっと、僕のペンのインクがきれちゃったよ。

ex.en: Oops, my fault. It's 3000 yen, not 3000 euros.
ex.ja: あ、間違えた。3000ユーロじゃなくて3000円ね。

note.ja: 驚き・失敗のときの間投詞。擬声語。

en: An agreement; a compact; a covenant.
An agreement between two or more nations.
To form a pact; to agree formally.

pact.ety: From Middle English pact, from Middle French pacte, from Old French, and its etymon Latin pactum (“something agreed upon”), from pacīscī (“to agree”).

ex.en: Let's make a pact.
ex.ja: ゆびきりげんまん。

ex.en: The EC countries are working out a new security pact.
ex.ja: ＥＣ諸国は新たな安全保障条約を検討中です。

ex.en: We made a pact that we wouldn't abandon one another.
ex.ja: 我々は互いに相手を見捨てないと約束した。

note.ja: ラテン語 pactum（合意）から。pacisci（取り決める）。「協定」。peace と同じ祖先。

en: Of, related to, or suffering from clinical paranoia.
Exhibiting excessive fear, suspicion, or distrust.
A person suffering from paranoia.

From paranoia + -oid.

note.ja: paranoia + -oid。ギリシャ語 para（そばに・外れて）+ nous（心）。「心が外れた」→「被害妄想の」。

en: One who protects or supports; a defender or advocate.
A guardian or intercessor; synonym of patron saint.

patron.ety: From Middle English patroun, patrone, from Old French patron, from Latin patrōnus, derived from pater (“father”). Doublet of padrone, Patronus, patroon, and pattern.

ex.en: He's been a patron of this store for many years.
ex.ja: あの人はこの店の長年の馴染み客です。

ex.en: The patron appreciates genuine antiques.
ex.ja: その後援者は本物の骨董品の良さが分かる。

note.ja: ラテン語 patronus（保護者）から。patr（父）。父のように守る人 →「後援者・常連客」。

en: A snack food made from corn or maize kernels popped by dry heating.
A variety of corn or maize with a hard outer hull that, along with the type of starch it contains, makes it suitable for popping.
To stand or jump up quickly.
To pop repeatedly, like popcorn cooking.

popcorn.ety: Short for popped corn. By surface analysis, pop + corn.

ex.en: Would you like some more salt on your popcorn?
ex.ja: ポップコーンにもう少し塩を入れましょうか？

ex.en: The more popcorn you eat, the more you want.
ex.ja: ポップコーンは食べれば食べるほどもっと食べたくなる。

ex.en: Tom put the bowl of popcorn on the table.
ex.ja: トムはポップコーンの入ったボウルを、テーブルの上に置いた。

note.ja: pop（ポンとはじける）+ corn（トウモロコシ）。「はじけるトウモロコシ」。

zh: 代理服務器 /代理服务器

en: Used as a proxy or acting as a proxy.
An agent or substitute authorized to act for another person.
The authority to act for another, especially when written.
To serve as a proxy for.
To function as a server for a client device, but pass on the requests to another server for service.

proxy.ety: Inherited from Middle English procucie, contraction of procuracie, from Anglo-Norman procuracie, from Medieval Latin procuratia, from Latin prōcūrātiō, from Latin prōcūrō (“to manage, administer”) (English procure). Compare proctor.

note.ja: procuracy（代理）の短縮。ラテン語 procurare（世話をする）。「代理（人）」。procure（調達する）と同じ。

en: Of a measurements and data types: based on some quantity or number rather than on some quality.
Of logical analysis: based on quantification as well as qualification, rather than solely the latter: thus, not ignorant of magnitudes (l…

quantitative.ety: From Late Latin quantitātīvus. By surface analysis, quantity + -ative.

note.ja: quantity（量）+ -ative。ラテン語 quantus（どれほど大きい）。「量的な」。qualitative（質的な）と対。

en: To get back; to recover possession of.
The act or process of regaining something.
The amount of width a woven cloth grows by when the fibers swell, used to determine the width of the reed to use in weaving.

regain.ety: From Middle French regaigner (French regagner). By surface analysis, re- + gain.

ex.en: I hope your mother will regain her health soon.
ex.ja: お母さま、早く健康を取り戻されるといいですね。

ex.en: I have finally regained my regular form.
ex.ja: やっと本調子を取り戻した。

ex.en: The man regained the use of his left arm.
ex.ja: その男は左の腕が再び動くようになった。

note.ja: re（再び）+ gain（得る）。「取り戻す」。

en: To make (something) new again; to restore to freshness or original condition.
To replace (something which has broken etc.); to replenish (something which has been exhausted), to keep up a required supply of.
Synonym of renewal.

renew.ety: From Middle English renewen, an alteration (possibly on analogy with Latin renovāre) of earlier anewen (“to renew”), from Old English nīewian (“to restore; renovate; renew”), equivalent to re- + new. Cognate with Old High German giniuwōn (“to renew”), Middle High German geniuwen (“to renew”), Old Norse nýja (“to renew”).

ex.en: He asked me to renew the bond.
ex.ja: 彼は私に証書を書き換えるよう要求した。

ex.en: I had my driver's license renewed last month.
ex.ja: 私は先月、運転免許証を更新してもらった。

ex.en: This medicine renews your strength.
ex.ja: この薬は活力を補給してくれます。

note.ja: re（再び）+ new（新しい）。「新たにする・更新する」。

en: To be like or similar to (something); to represent as similar.

resemble.ety: From Middle English resemblen, from Anglo-Norman resembler, ressembler, from re- + sembler (“to seem”). By surface analysis, re- + semble.

ex.en: This is a dog that resembles a horse.
ex.ja: これは馬ににている犬です。

ex.en: Seen from the Moon, Earth resembles a ball.
ex.ja: 月から見ると、地球はボールのように見える。

ex.en: Its long neck resembles that of a horse.
ex.ja: その長い首は馬に似ている。

note.ja: re（強く）+ sembl（似ている）+ e。よく似ている →「〜に似ている」。similar と同じ祖先。

en: Of, or relating to, the past, past times, or the way things were.
Affecting things past; retroactive, ex post facto.
Past fashions or trends.
A chess puzzle of retrograde analysis, requiring the solver to work out the history of moves leading to the position presented.

retro.ety: Borrowed from French rétro, ultimately from Latin retro.

ex.en: The retro feel of this cafe is a hit with young people.
ex.ja: この喫茶店は、独特のレトロさが若者にうけている。

note.ja: フランス語 rétro（retrospective の短縮）から。ラテン語 retro（後ろへ）。「懐古的な」。

en: To rebel, particularly against authority.
To repel greatly.
An act of revolting.

revolt.ety:
Borrowed from French révolter, from Italian rivoltare, itself either from ri- with the verb voltare, or possibly from a Vulgar Latin *revoltāre < *revolvitāre, for *revolūtāre, frequentative of Latin revolvō (“roll back”) (through its past participle revolūtus).
Compare typologically Russian переворо́т (perevorót) (akin to верте́ть (vertétʹ).

ex.en: The army had the revolt well in hand.
ex.ja: 軍隊は反乱を制圧した。

ex.en: Human nature revolts against such a crime.
ex.ja: 人間ならだれでもそんな罪悪に対して不快感を持つ。

ex.en: People rose in revolt against the king.
ex.ja: 民衆は国王に対して反乱を起こした。

note.ja: re（逆に）+ volt（回る）。向きをひっくり返す →「反乱（を起こす）・反感を抱かせる」。revolution と同じ volv。

en: In a right manner; correctly, justifiably.

rightly.ety: From Middle English ryȝtly, rihtliche, from Old English rihtlīċe, from Proto-West Germanic *rehtalīkā, *rehtalīkō, from Proto-Germanic *rehtalīkê, *rehtalīkô (“rightly”), equivalent to right + -ly. Cognate with West Frisian rjochtlik, Dutch rechtelijk, German rechtlich, Swedish rätteligen, Icelandic réttilega.

ex.en: He is, quite rightly, very grateful to them.
ex.ja: 彼は、きわめて当然のことだが、彼らにとても感謝している。

ex.en: They are cousins, if I remember rightly.
ex.ja: 私の記憶が確かなら彼らはいとこ同士だ。

ex.en: He was rightly punished.
ex.ja: 彼は罰せられたが、それは当然のことだ。

note.ja: right（正しい）+ -ly。「正しく・当然」。

en: A seat for a rider, typically made of leather and raised in the front and rear, placed on the back of a horse or other animal, and secure…
A similar implement used to secure goods to animals; a packsaddle.
To put a saddle (noun sense 1) on (an animal).
To put (something) on to another thing like a saddle on an animal.

saddle.ety:
From Middle English sadel, from Old English sadol, from Proto-West Germanic *sadul, from Proto-Germanic *sadulaz (“saddle”). Further etymology uncertain, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *sod-dʰlo-, from *sed- (“to sit”) + *-dʰlom (a variant of *-trom (suffix forming nouns denoting instruments or tools)), though the Oxford English Dictionary says this “presents formal difficulties”.

ex.en: Don't put the saddle on the wrong horse.
ex.ja: お門違いですよ。

ex.en: Can you ride without a saddle?
ex.ja: サドルなしで乗れるの？

ex.en: She saddled him with the work.
ex.ja: 彼女はその仕事を彼に課した。

note.ja: 古英語 sadol から。sit（座る）と同系。「鞍」→ 重荷を「負わせる」。

en: A holy or sacred place dedicated to a specific deity, ancestor, hero, martyr, saint, or similar figure of awe and respect, at which said …
A case, box, or receptacle, especially one in which are deposited sacred relics, as the bones of a saint.
To enshrine; to place reverently, as if in a shrine.

shrine.ety: From Middle English shryne, from Old English scrīn (“reliquary, ark of the covenant”), from Medieval Latin scrīnium (“reliquary”), “case or chest for books or papers” in Classical Latin. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to turn, bend”). Compare Old Norse skrín, Old High German skrīni (German Schrein).

ex.en: This path will lead you to the shrine.
ex.ja: この道は神社へ通じていますよ。

ex.en: The shrine was built two hundred years ago.
ex.ja: その神社は２００年前に建てられた。

ex.en: The old shrine used to stand there.
ex.ja: その古い神社は以前はそこにありました。

note.ja: ラテン語 scrinium（書類箱）から。聖遺物を入れた箱 →「聖地・廟」。日本の「神社」にも使う。

en: To cause to become smaller.
To become smaller; to contract.
Shrinkage; contraction; recoil.
Loss of inventory, for example due to shoplifting or not selling items before their expiration date.

shrink.ety:
From Middle English schrynken, from Old English sċrincan, from Proto-Germanic *skrinkwaną. Cognate with Dutch schrinken (“to shrink”).
The sense “psychologist, psychotherapist” is a clipping of head-shrinker.

ex.en: He shrank back in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面してしり込みした。

ex.en: I felt as if he shrank from meeting me.
ex.ja: 彼は僕に会うのを避けたように思った。

ex.en: The population of Japan is shrinking.
ex.ja: 日本の人口は先細りしています。

note.ja: 古英語 scrincan（縮む）から。「縮む」→ 頭を縮める精神科医を俗に shrink と言う。

en: A person using long-range small arms for precise attacks from a concealed position.
A sniper rifle.

sniper.ety:

ex.ja: 狙撃兵は白いヴァンを運転している。

en: One who lives alone, or in solitude; an anchorite, hermit or recluse.
The state of being solitary; solitude
Living or being by oneself; alone; having no companion present
Performed, passed, or endured alone.

solitary.ety: From Middle English solitarie, borrowed from Latin sōlitārius. Doublet of solitaire.

ex.en: He likes to take a solitary walk.
ex.ja: 彼は一人で散歩をするのが好きだ。

ex.en: She led a solitary life.
ex.ja: 彼女は孤独な生活を送った。

ex.en: She lives a solitary life in a remote part of Scotland.
ex.ja: 彼女はスコットランドの辺ぴなところで孤独な暮らしをしている。

note.ja: ラテン語 solus（ひとりの）から。sole、solo と同じ。「ひとりの・孤独な」。

en: unhappiness, woe
(usually in plural) An instance or cause of unhappiness.
To feel or express grief.
To feel grief over; to mourn, regret.

sorrow.ety: From Middle English sorwe, sorow, sorewe, from Old English sorg, sorh (“care, anxiety, sorrow, grief”), from Proto-West Germanic *sorgu, from Proto-Germanic *surgō (compare West Frisian soarch, Dutch zorg, German Sorge, Danish, Swedish and Norwegian sorg), from Proto-Indo-European *swergʰ- (“watch over, worry; be ill, suffer”) (compare Old Irish serg (“sickness”), Tocharian B sark (“sickness”), Lithuanian sirgti (“be sick”), Sanskrit सूर्क्षति (sū́rkṣati, “worry”). Despite the similarity in form and meaning, not historically related to sorry and sore.

ex.en: To my great sorrow, my father died young.
ex.ja: 大変悲しいことに父は若くして亡くなった。

ex.en: He felt great sorrow when his wife died.
ex.ja: 彼は妻が死んだとき大きな悲しみを感じた。

ex.en: Her death brought deep sorrow to the nation.
ex.ja: 彼女の死は国民に深い悲しみをもたらした。

note.ja: 古英語 sorg（悲しみ）から。sorry とは別語源だが意味の近さで似た形になった。

en: The process of terminating or the state of being terminated.
The process of firing an employee; ending one's employment at a business for any reason.

termination.ety: Borrowed from Latin terminationem (accusative of terminatio).

note.ja: terminate（終わらせる）+ -ion。ラテン語 terminus（境界・終点）。「終了・解約」。term、terminal と同じ。

en: The upper leg of a human, between the hip and the knee.
That part of the leg of vertebrates (or sometimes other animals) which corresponds to the human thigh in position or function; the tibia …

thigh.ety:

From Middle English thigh, thegh, thiȝ, theȝhe, þigh, þyȝh, from Old English þēoh, þīoh, from Proto-West Germanic *þeuh, from Proto-Germanic *þeuhą, from Proto-Indo-European *tewk-. ex.en: What's the difference between chicken breast and chicken thigh?
ex.ja: 鶏肉のムネとモモってどう違うの？

ex.en: You need to have strong thigh muscles to skate.
ex.ja: スケートをするには強い腿の筋肉が必要である。

ex.en: She has a tattoo of a lizard on her thigh.
ex.ja: 彼女はももにトカゲの入れ墨がついています。

note.ja: 古英語 thēoh から。「太もも」。gh は発音しない。

en: To grow or increase stature; to grow vigorously or luxuriantly; to enjoy a state of excellent health and well-being; to flourish.
To increase in wealth or success; to prosper, be profitable.

thrive.ety: From Middle English thryven, thriven, from Old Norse þrífa (“to seize, grasp, take hold, prosper”), from Proto-Germanic *þrībaną (“to seize, prosper”), from Proto-Indo-European *trep-, *terp- (“to satisfy, enjoy”). Cognate with Swedish trivas, Danish trives, Norwegian Bokmål trives.

ex.en: His business has begun to thrive at last.
ex.ja: 彼の事業もやっと萌芽の兆しを見せた。

ex.en: First thrive and then take a wife.
ex.ja: まず商売を繁昌させてから妻をめとれ。

ex.en: He that will thrive must ask leave of his wife.
ex.ja: 成功するおっとは妻の許可を求めるものだ。

note.ja: 北欧語 þrífask（つかむ・栄える）から。「繁栄する・すくすく育つ」。

en: a giant supernatural being, especially a grotesque humanoid creature living in caves or hills or under bridges.
An optical ejection from the top of the electrically active core region of a thunderstorm that is red in colour and seems to occur after …
To move (something, especially a round object) by, or as if by, rolling; to bowl, to roll, to trundle.
To roll; also, to turn round and round; to rotate, to spin, to whirl.

troll.ety:
Partly:
* from Middle English trol (“demon (?); sorcerer (?)”) [and other forms], from Old Norse trǫll (“conjurer, mage; witch”), from Proto-Germanic *truzlą (“supernatural being; demon, fiend; giant; monster”), probably from *trudaną (“to step on; to tread”) + *-ilą (suffix forming agent nouns); and
* borrowed from Norwegian Bokmål troll, Swedish troll, or Danish trold, from Old Norse trǫll (see above).
Doublet of droll and trow.
Cognates
* Danish fortrylle (“to bewitch”), trylle (“to conjure”)
* Icelandic tröll
* Middle High German trol, crewtrolle (“spook, wraith; ogre, monster”)
* Norwegia

ex.en: Trolling is a art.
ex.ja: 釣りね芸術の一つ。

ex.en: Don't feed the troll!
ex.ja: ネタにマジレスするな。

ex.en: I just don't understand what goes through the minds of people who troll forums.
ex.ja: 掲示板を荒らす人の精神状態がわかりません。

note.ja: 北欧神話の巨人・妖精トロルから。「（ネットで）荒らし」は釣りの trolling（流し釣り）とも結びついた。

en: Not covered or protected from the weather, etc.
Lacking insurance or security.

uncovered.ety: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

ex.en: How many new sites were uncovered?
ex.ja: 新しい遺跡で未発掘はいくつだったのですか。

ex.en: Investigators uncovered an assassination plot.
ex.ja: 捜査員らは暗殺計画を摘発しました。

note.ja: uncover（覆いを取る）+ -ed。「覆いのない」→「明らかにされた」。

ex.ja: 料金滞納で電話を止められた。

en: Failed, not successful.

ex.ja: 試みはだいたいにおいて失敗だった。

ex.en: That plan was unsuccessful.
ex.ja: その計画は失敗に終わった。

ex.en: Our plan was unsuccessful.
ex.ja: 我々の計画は失敗した。

note.ja: un（否定）+ successful（成功した）。「失敗した」。

en: A sleeveless garment that buttons down the front, worn over a shirt, and often as part of a suit; a waistcoat.
A sleeveless garment, often with a low-cut neck, usually worn under a shirt or blouse.
To clothe with, or as with, a vestment, or garment; to dress; to robe; to cover, surround, or encompass closely.
To clothe with authority, power, etc.; to put in possession; to invest; to furnish; to endow; followed by with and the thing conferred.

vest.ety: Derived from French veste (“a vest, jacket”), from Latin vestis (“a garment, gown, robe, vestment, clothing, vesture”), from Proto-Indo-European *wéstis, from *wes- (“to be dressed”) (English wear). Cognate with Sanskrit वस्त्र (vastra) and Spanish vestir.

ex.en: Men don't wear vests much these days.
ex.ja: 最近、男の人はあまりベストを着ない。

ex.en: You need to reverse your vest. It's inside-out!
ex.ja: ベストを裏返さなくちゃ。表裏逆ですよ。

ex.en: You need to reverse your vest, it's back to front.
ex.ja: ベストを裏返さなくちゃ。表裏逆ですよ。

note.ja: イタリア語 veste（衣服）から。ラテン語 vestis。investigate とは別だが、invest（服を着せる → 投資する）、vestment（法衣）と同じ。

en: Any plant whose stem requires support and which climbs by tendrils or twining.
Any plant the stem of which creeps along the ground.

vine.ety: From Middle English vyne, from Anglo-Norman vigne, from Vulgar Latin vīnia, from Latin vīnea (“vines in a vineyard”), from vīneus (“related to wine”), from vīnum (“wine”), from Proto-Italic *wīnom, from Proto-Indo-European *wóyh₁nom (“vine, wine”), from *weh₁y- (“to twist, wrap”). Doublet of wine.

ex.en: There is a dense growth of vines in this forest.
ex.ja: この森には野ブドウが密集して生えている。

ex.en: You don't get eggplants from a gourd vine.
ex.ja: 瓜のつるに茄子はならぬ。

ex.en: This vine winds around trees.
ex.ja: このつる草は木にからみつきます。

note.ja: ラテン語 vinea（ブドウ畑）から。vinum（ワイン）。「ブドウの木」→「つる」。wine、vinegar（酸っぱいワイン）と同じ。

en: A guarantee that a certain outcome or obligation will be fulfilled; security.
A legal agreement, either written or oral (an expressed warranty) or implied through the actions of the buyer and seller (an implied warr…
To warrant; to guarantee.

warranty.ety: From Middle English warantye, warantie, from Anglo-Norman warrantie, an Old Northern French variant of Old French guarantie (Modern French garantie). Doublet of guarantee and guaranty. More at warrant.

note.ja: 古北フランス語 warantie（保証）から。guarantee と同じ語源（w と gu の対応）。「保証」。

en: Reduced; made less strong.

ex.en: Our competitive position is weakened by the rising labor cost.
ex.ja: 労働コストの上昇で、我々の競争力は弱まっている。

ex.en: My muscular strength has weakened from lack of exercise.
ex.ja: 運動不足で筋肉が弱くなった。

ex.en: Tom has a weakened immune system.
ex.ja: トムは免疫力が低下している。

note.ja: weaken（弱める）+ -ed。「弱まった」。

en: The unit of Japanese currency (symbol: ¥) since 1871, divided into 100 sen.
A coin or note worth one yen.
To have a strong desire for.

yen.ety: From Medhurst and Hepburn’s romanizations, under the influence of earlier Portuguese romanizations, of Japanese 圓(えん) (en, “round; a round object”) as ye or yen, now 円(えん) (en), from Chinese 銀圓 /银圆 (yínyuán, “round silver object(s), especially a piece of eight”): 銀 /银 (yín, “silver”) + 圓 /圆 (yuán, “circular, round; yuan, yen, dollar”). Cognate with Chinese 元 (yuán, “monetary unit, especially RMB”) and Korean 원 (won, “North or South Korean won”). Doublet of won and yuan.

ex.en: This desk cost me no more than 30000 yen.
ex.ja: この机はたった３００００円だった。

ex.en: This desk cost me no less than 30000 yen.
ex.ja: この机は３００００円もした。

ex.en: He had only one hundred yen on him.
ex.ja: 彼は百円しか持ち合わせていなかった。

note.ja: 「円」は日本語から。「あこがれ」は中国語（広東語）yan（渇望）からで別語。

en: The trachea.
The trachea and bronchial tree.

en: A wing of a building, notably in a church separated from the nave proper by piers.
A clear path/passage through rows of seating.

aisle.ety:
From Middle English ele, from Anglo-Norman ele (“wing”) (Modern French aile), from Latin āla (whence English ala). Further from Latin axis (whence English axis, atelier). Via Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱs- cognate with English axle, Ancient Greek ἄξων (áxōn) (whence English axo-, axon).
The modern pronunciation has been influenced by English isle, whence the obsolete form isle; the modern spelling reflects further modification of this form after modern French aile.

ex.en: His seat in the plane was on the aisle.
ex.ja: 機内での彼の席は通路側だった。

ex.en: Would you prefer a window or an aisle seat?
ex.ja: 席は窓側、通路側のどちらがよろしいですか？

ex.en: Don't put your stuff in the aisle.
ex.ja: 通路に物を置くな。

note.ja: 古フランス語 ele（翼）から。教会の側廊（翼の部分）→「通路」。s は island と同じく後から入った。

en: Unlimited in might; omnipotent; all-powerful
Having very great power, influence, etc.

almighty.ety: From Middle English almyghty, almighty, from Old English ælmihtiġ (“all-powerful”), from Proto-Germanic *alamahtīgaz, equivalent to al- + might + -y.

ex.en: Man is not as almighty as God.
ex.ja: 人間は神ほど万能ではない。

note.ja: all（すべて）+ mighty（力のある）。「全能の」。

en: Clothing.
Aspect, guise, form.
To dress or clothe; to attire.
To furnish with apparatus; to equip; to fit out.

apparel.ety: From Old French apareillier. Doublet of parrel.

ex.en: The queen was richly appareled.
ex.ja: 女王は豪華な服装をしていた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 apareillier（準備する）から。「装備」→「衣服・アパレル」。apparatus と同系。

A process through which two or more parties use an arbitrator or arbiter in order to resolve a dispute.

ex.ja: 仲裁では普通６ヶ月に裁決を下す。

note.ja: arbitrate（仲裁する）+ -ion。ラテン語 arbiter（審判者）。「仲裁」。arbitrary と同じ。

An object made or shaped by some agent or intelligence, not necessarily of direct human origin.

ex.ja: その博物館にはケルト時代の文化遺産のすばらしいコレクションがある。

ex.en: That museum has a superb collection of Celtic era cultural artifacts.
ex.ja: その博物館にはケルト時代の文化遺産のすばらしいコレクションがある。

note.ja: ラテン語 arte factum（技で作られたもの）。「人工物・遺物」。art、fact と同じ。

en: A dark reddish-brown colour, often used to describe hair colour.
Of a reddish-brown colour.

auburn.ety: Early Modern English auburn (“brown, reddish brown”) from Middle English aubourne, abron, abroune, abrune (“light brown, yellowish brown, blond”), alteration (due to conflation with Middle English brun (“brown”)) of earlier auborne (“yellowish-white, flaxen”) from Old French auborne, alborne (“blond, flaxen, off-white”) from Medieval Latin alburnus (“whitish”), from Latin albus (“white”). More at albino, brown.

note.ja: ラテン語 alburnus（白っぽい）から。のちに brown と混同されて「赤褐色の」になった。

en: Rousing from sleep, in a natural or a figurative sense; rousing into activity; exciting
The act of awaking, or ceasing to sleep.
A revival of religion, or more general attention to religious matters than usual.

note.ja: awaken（目覚める）+ -ing。「目覚め・覚醒」。

en: Having two sides.
Involving both sides equally.
A meeting between two people or groups.

ex.en: What will become of our close relations if the bilateral security treaty expires?
ex.ja: 相互安全保障条約が期限切れになったら、両国の親密な関係はどうなるだろう？

note.ja: bi（2つの）+ lateral（側の）。「二国間の・双方の」。

en: To shed blood through an injured blood vessel.
To menstruate.
An incident of bleeding, as in haemophilia.
A system for tapping hot, high-pressure air from a gas turbine engine for purposes such as cabin pressurization and airframe anti-icing.

bleed.ety:
From Middle English bleden, from Old English blēdan (“to bleed”), from Proto-West Germanic *blōdijan, from Proto-Germanic *blōdijaną (“to bleed”), from *blōþą (“blood”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots blede, bleid (“to bleed”), Saterland Frisian bläide (“to bleed”), West Frisian bliede (“to bleed”), Dutch bloeden (“to bleed”), Low German blöden (“to bleed”), German bluten (“to bleed”), Danish bløde (“to bleed”), Swedish blöda (“to bleed”).

ex.en: With a weak beat, it continues to bleed.
ex.ja: 臆病な鼓動とともに血はにじみ続ける。

ex.en: I bleed easily when I am cut.
ex.ja: 指を切るとすぐ血が出る。

ex.en: She bled me of all my money.
ex.ja: 彼女は私からすっかり金をしぼり取った。

note.ja: 古英語 blēdan から。blood（血）と同じ。「出血する」。

en: A curved instrument or handle of iron or wood, for holding and turning bits, etc.; a bitstock.
That which holds anything tightly or supports it firmly; a bandage or a prop.
To prepare for something bad, such as an impact or blow.
To place in a position for resisting pressure; to hold firmly.

brace.ety: From Middle English brace, from Old French brace (“arm”), from Latin bracchia, the nominative and accusative plural of bracchium (“arm”).

ex.en: I braced myself against the crowd.
ex.ja: 群衆に押されないよう力を入れて踏ん張った。

ex.en: Since she got her braces, I've hardly seen her smile.
ex.ja: 歯にブリッジを入れてから、ほとんど彼女の笑顔を見なくなった。

ex.en: I think I need braces.
ex.ja: 歯列矯正をお願いしたいのですが。

note.ja: ラテン語 bracchia（両腕）から。「両腕で抱える」→「支え・身構える」、歯を支える器具 →「歯列矯正器」。bracelet（腕輪）も同じ。

en: The descriptive heading or title, of a document or part thereof.
A title or brief explanation attached to an illustration, cartoon, user interface element, etc.
To add captions to a text or illustration.
To add captions to a film or broadcast.

caption.ety: Borrowed from Latin captiō (“deception, fraud”), from the past participle of capiō (“to take, to seize”) (English capture). Compare Middle English capcioun (“seizure, capture”).

ex.en: Put a caption on this photo.
ex.ja: この写真にタイトルをつけて。

note.ja: ラテン語 captio（つかむこと）から。cap（つかむ）。（内容をつかむ）見出し →「見出し・説明文・字幕」。

en: To be unable to breathe because of obstruction of the windpipe (for instance food or other objects that go down the wrong way, or fumes o…
To prevent (someone) from breathing or talking by strangling or filling the windpipe.
A control on a carburetor to adjust the air/fuel mixture when the engine is cold.
In wrestling, karate (etc.), a type of hold that can result in strangulation.

choke.ety: From Middle English choken (also cheken), from earlier acheken, from Old English āċēocian (“to choke”), probably derived from Old English ċēoce, ċēace (“jaw, cheek”), see cheek. Cognate with Icelandic kok (“throat”), koka (“to gulp”). See also achoke.

ex.en: For some reason I choke whenever I drink something.
ex.ja: 飲み物を飲むときなぜか必ずむせる。

ex.en: She can't talk about her mother without choking up.
ex.ja: 彼女は母親の事を話するときはいつもむせび泣きする。

ex.en: I'll choke the life out of him.
ex.ja: あいつの息の根を止めてやる。

note.ja: 古英語 ācēocian（息を詰まらせる）から。cheek（ほお・あご）と同系とされる。

en: A sterol lipid synthesized by the liver and transported in the bloodstream to the membranes of all animal cells; it plays a central role …
The level of cholesterol in the body.

ex.ja: コレステロール値が高いのです。

ex.en: If you want to avoid cholesterol, eat lean meat with no fat.
ex.ja: コレステロールをためたくなかったら、脂肪のない赤身の肉を食べるのがよい。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kholē（胆汁）+ stereos（固い）+ -ol。胆石から見つかったことから。

en: Elegant, highly stylish or fashionable.
Of a superior type; especially, exhibiting admirable personal qualities.

classy.ety: From class + -y. Piecewise doublet of classic.

ex.en: Miss, that dress is splendid, it has a sheer silhouette and is very classy.
ex.ja: お客さま、そちらのドレスはすとんとしたシルエットがとても上品で素敵なんです。

note.ja: class（上流・品格）+ -y。「上品な・高級な」。

ex.en: I was compelled to do the work alone.
ex.ja: 私は一人でその仕事を無理矢理させられた。

ex.ja: 戦争で兵士達は戦線に行かざるをえなかった。

ex.en: He was compelled to sign the contract.
ex.ja: 彼は無理にその契約に署名させられた。

Of a meld; completed without calling another player's discarded tile unless that call would complete the hand.

ex.ja: 彼女は彼に対する感情の変化を隠した。

ex.ja: 彼はその本を上着の下に隠した。

ex.en: He concealed his poverty from my eyes.
ex.ja: 彼は貧しさを私の眼につかないようにした。

note.ja: conceal（隠す）+ -ed。con + celare（隠す）。「隠された」。cell と同系。

en: The act of confronting or challenging another, especially face to face.
A conflict between armed forces.

ex.en: He deliberately kept on provoking a confrontation.
ex.ja: 彼は対立を引き起こそうと、わざとしつこくした。

en: A benefactor; someone who donates to charity or some cause.
A person who backs, supports or champions a cause, activity or institution.

contributor.ety: From Anglo-Norman contributour (from Latin contribuō); equivalent to contribute + -or.

ex.en: I hope you become an advanced contributor.
ex.ja: 上級ユーザーになってくれたらいいのにな。

note.ja: con（共に）+ trib（割り当てる）+ utor。分け与える人 →「貢献者・寄稿者」。

en: Very fine in quality or luxurious.
Something that is deluxe.

deluxe.ety: Borrowed from French de luxe (“of luxury”), from Latin luxus (“excess”).
